Playing it
Keys
Mouse, touch or the computer keyboard. Where you hit a key sets its velocity: near the front is loud, near the back is soft. A S D F G H J K L ; ' are the white keys from F, W E R Y U O P [ the black ones.
Knobs
The FM-1's encoders are endless and click. Switch between sliders and knobs at the top. A knob turns with a drag up or down, the wheel, or the ‹ › buttons (one click each). A slider jumps straight to a value when the firmware tells the simulator what the knob is tied to (h1 does); otherwise it turns the encoder as far as you drag and springs back. , . SELECT, ← → PRESETS, ↑ ↓ ALGORITHM, 1–4 the four knobs (with Shift to turn down).
Buttons
Labelled the way the running firmware names them. Hold one with the mouse or a finger as long as you like. To press two at once, Shift-click the first (dashed outline), then click the second: they go down together and come up together, as with two fingers (h1's SEQ + REC). Shift-click one and then turn an encoder or play a key, and it stays held until you click it again (EDIT + SELECT). Z X are OCT − and OCT +.
MASTER
The volume pot, passed to the firmware the way the device reads it.
MIDI in
Plays the firmware from a MIDI keyboard or a DAW through Web MIDI (Chrome, Edge, Firefox).
My FM-1
Plays it from a real FM-1 running RemoteFM1 (0.3 or later), plugged in over USB: its keys, buttons, encoders and MASTER work this panel, and the page's screen and lights show on its own. Chrome or Edge, which ask to allow MIDI with SysEx. Turn the FM-1's own volume down; the sound comes from here.
About this firmware 

      

      

      

    

  


  

    What a simulator can and can't tell you
    

      
The sound and the picture come from the firmware's own code, compiled for the browser, driven one device millisecond at a time with the same 44.1 kHz audio blocks and 15 ms frames the FM-1 runs. Saves go to a flash image kept in this browser, so a firmware remembers its settings between visits.

      
What it can't show: how hard the FM-1's own processor is working, how the speaker sounds, and how the keys and encoders feel. An .rfm1 is a firmware's host build, so code that only runs on the chip (its drivers, Bluetooth, USB) is not in it. Try a firmware here, then flash the device build with its own installer. This simulator is open source: fm1-browser-simulator on GitHub.
